text: Given 5 active eligible technicians in a queue, each starting at 0 open tickets, when 10 tickets are assigned concurrently via autotask_assign_least_loaded_resource, then every technician ends up with exactly 2 tickets (max-min spread across technicians <= 1)
evidence: npx jest tests/assign-least-loaded.test.ts -- exit 0, 7/7 passed (2026-10-21). This case asserts tickets.length===10 and every resource's final count===2 (spread [2,2,2,2,2]) after Promise.all of 10 concurrent callTool() invocations against a stateful routed-fetch mock backed by a real AutotaskService+AutotaskToolHandler.

text: Given a queue has exactly 1 active eligible technician, when 5 tickets are assigned, then all 5 go to that technician and no call errors
evidence: npx jest tests/assign-least-loaded.test.ts -- exit 0, 7/7 passed (2026-10-21). This case asserts isError is falsy and assignedResourceID equals the sole resource on all 5 sequential calls, and tickets.length===5 all assigned to it.

text: Given 3 eligible technicians with existing open-ticket counts of 5, 0, and 3, when 1 new ticket is assigned, then it goes to the technician with count 0
evidence: npx jest tests/assign-least-loaded.test.ts -- exit 0, 7/7 passed (2026-10-21). This case pre-seeds the mock's ticket list with 5/0/3 open tickets per resource, asserts the chosen assignedResourceID is the count-0 resource, and asserts the returned consideredResources array reports {5,0,3} per resource.

text: Given two assignment calls for the same queue are issued so their internal counting steps would overlap without serialization, when both complete, then the second call's decision reflects the first call's result, not a stale snapshot -- the two calls never both pick the same resource off the same count
evidence: npx jest tests/assign-least-loaded.test.ts -- exit 0, 7/7 passed (2026-10-21). This case gates call A's Tickets/query (open-ticket count read) behind a manually-released promise, fires call B synchronously right after A with nothing awaited in between, then asserts via 3 drained microtask ticks that call B has made zero fetch calls and zero tickets exist yet (proving the lock -- not timing luck -- is what prevents B from starting). After releasing the gate, asserts A picked resourceID 501 and B picked 502 (never the same resource), and that more fetch calls happened after release than before it.

text: Given a queue has zero active eligible technicians, when a ticket is assigned, then the tool throws a distinct NoEligibleResourceError and neither createTicket nor updateTicket is called
evidence: npx jest tests/assign-least-loaded.test.ts -- exit 0, 7/7 passed (2026-10-21). This case asserts result.isError===true, the serialized error message matches new NoEligibleResourceError(queueID).message exactly, and that the mock recorded no POST /Tickets and no PATCH /Tickets/777 call.

text: Given a live Autotask sandbox/INT queue with 3 or more active technicians, when 5 test-prefixed tickets are created through autotask_assign_least_loaded_resource, then the Autotask UI shows assignees spread per the least-open-count rule and each assignedResourceID matches what the tool reported
steps: In INT/staging with real Autotask credentials, identify a queue with 3 or more active technicians
Call autotask_assign_least_loaded_resource 5 times with a clearly test-prefixed ticket title
Open the queue in the Autotask UI and record each ticket's assignee
Compare against the tool's reported assignedResourceID for each call
expect: Assignees are spread (no single technician holds more than ceil(5/3)=2 of the 5 tickets) and the UI's assignee matches the tool's reported assignedResourceID for every ticket
evidence: NOT EXECUTED: this sandbox has no AUTOTASK_USERNAME/AUTOTASK_SECRET credentials; needs dev/QA with live Autotask access after implementation.
